rulings.reason: The instruction scores only whether a release sentence or link appears in the abstract, not whether any artifact exists, works, or supports the claims, so a 10 is awarded for a piece of boilerplate a judge can detect without reading the science. Routed B, but mixed because open-release practice plausibly co-occurs with more rigorous and better-resourced work.

The text explicitly brackets out how positive or well-supported the figures are, reducing the criterion to counting numerals and units, so an abstract padded with unsupported or trivial numbers outscores one with a single decisive result. Routed B, but mixed because genuinely careful empirical work tends to report checkable quantities.

It scores the presence of a rhetorical opening device -- a posed question or a 'prior work suggests X, but...' construction -- and explicitly contrasts it with plainly stated contributions, so it rewards packaging rather than any actual resolution of a field tension. Routed B, but mixed because real engagement with an open question is one plausible upstream cause of that framing.
